column1: # Requirements for Mica::Brotli (milestone Z4, the pure-Crystal Brotli
# decoder): the decoder requirements of RFC 7932, the public API and the
# decode limits. The differential campaign against google/brotli 1.2.1
# encoder emits and the rejection of mutated streams.

column3: The 122,784-byte static dictionary is embedded byte for byte, with NDBITS and DOFFSET per word length
The 121 word transforms (prefix, elementary transform, suffix) are embedded in transform-ID order
Every conformance file of google/brotli v1.2.1 decodes to its original, one-shot and streaming
WBITS 10 to 24 are decoded from the stream header
The large-window marker (an extension outside RFC 7932) is rejected
Uncompressed metablocks are copied after byte alignment
Metadata metablocks are skipped and produce no output, including as the last metablock (as libbrotlidec does)
A metablock length of 5 or 6 nibbles whose last nibble is zero, or a metadata length whose last byte is zero, is rejected
Padding bits before uncompressed and metadata contents and after the last metablock must be zero
A simple prefix code that lists a symbol twice or a symbol outside the alphabet is rejected
Inserts, copies and dictionary words that run past their metablock are rejected
Back references copy from the window, overlapping copies included
Short distance codes that give a distance below 1 are rejected
Distances beyond the window address static dictionary words and their transforms
Bytes after the last metablock are rejected
Input that ends inside a stream raises TruncatedStreamError
The Reader gives the one-shot result for every input chunking and read size, across ring wraps
Output stops at max_output_bytes before the next byte is written
Output beyond max_ratio times the input consumed is stopped once it passes 1 MiB
A window above max_window_bytes is refused before any buffer is allocated
Metadata beyond max_metadata_bytes is refused
The work budget and the deadline stop a decode
The Reader's memory is bounded by the window, not by the output
